messages:
sara: Heads-up — noticed controller-manager in eu-central entering a repeated lease/leader loop since ~08:10 UTC. GPU provisioning jobs are getting stuck in Pending and we're falling back to hosted pools which is inflating costs.
ops-bot: [ALERT] ctrl-manager-eu-central leader-flap detected (alerts: leader-election-failure x5 in 10m)
mike: Can you paste the controller-manager logs? thinking it might be failing to renew the lease then frying the pod restarts.
sara: Pasted minimal excerpt below (redacted node ids):

```
I0321 08:09:57.123456       1 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out waiting for the condition
E0321 08:09:57.123567       1 controller_manager.go:112] controller-manager lost leader election lock: etcd request timed out
I0321 08:09:57.223456       1 server.go:200] shutting down leader-only controllers
I0321 08:09:58.345678       1 leaderelection.go:210] attempting to acquire leader lease  kube-system/controller-manager...
```

sara: Also seeing etcd tail latency spikes around same time: `etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds` 99th -> 2.3s for a few mins.
jin: We're definitely seeing API latencies + kube-scheduler backlog. Snapshot from 08:12:

```
$ kubectl get pods -n gpu-provisioning
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
gpu-provisioner-0                   0/1     Pending   0          4m
gpu-provisioner-1                   1/1     Running   0          39m
```

jin: Pending pods stuck on predicate `NoNodesAvailable` despite nodes showing allocatable GPUs — looks like controller-manager isn't reconciling node claims while leader is unstable.
mike: Two suspects: 1) controller-manager leader-election leaseDuration/renewDeadline values too tight for current etcd tail latency; 2) possibility of a zombie holder where lock wasn't properly released and manager keeps trying.
sara: Quick detection command I ran to find orphaned leases:

```
kubectl -n kube-system get lease -o wide | grep controller-manager
NAME                HOLDER               AGE
controller-manager  kube-controller-123   12m
```

sara: But the holder pod had restarted and new pod also trying to get the lease, so there was a short dual-contend period.
mike: Suggested fast mitigations:
- bump leaseDuration -> 60s and renewDeadline -> 40s in staging, then prod if it stabilizes
- temporarily increase etcd io and WAL durability headroom (move WAL to faster disk for 10m) if we can
- add a short canary: scale up a second controller-manager replica with leaderElection disabled to speed reconciliation? (risky)
jin: Cost note: fallback to hosted pools triggered ~120k tokens of model usage over the last 30m while provisioning was blocked. Rough incremental cost ~ $450 for that window. Ops wants us to minimize fallback windows.
sara: I spun a quick workaround: cordon node with flaky disk io, forced controller-manager onto healthier node, and restarted controller-manager (rolling). That reduced leader flaps. Reconciliation restarted and most Pending GPU pods moved to Running.
mike: Can we add a probe in the healthcheck to check lease renew success rate? If renew fails 3x in a row, auto-alert to oncall and mark slow-io tag on node.
jin: Agree. Also propose we add a small runbook section for "zombie lease / controller-manager leader looping" with commands and cost impact calc so finance can trace chargebacks.
sara: I'll draft the runbook and run the staged leaseDuration change in eu-central at 09:00 UTC. Assigning follow-ups:
- sara: draft runbook + rollout plan
- mike: validate leaseDuration change on staging and monitor etcd fsync metrics
- jin: add cost tag and notify finance after we have final numbers

ops-bot: incident-created: INC-20260321-312 (severity: low -> medium). Runbook link placeholder: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/zombie-lease

sara: Will update here after the staged test at 09:00. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
